topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course topic on the causes of cancer and outlines the learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Intrinsic and Genetic Drivers of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer develops as an evolutionary genetic disease driven by endogenous metabolic processes, replication errors, and inherited predispositions.

topics.label: Extrinsic Exposures and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine environmental risk factors, the debate surrounding intrinsic bad luck versus extrinsic exposure, and geographic variations in cancer incidence.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents contribute to oncogenesis, highlighting global pathogen links and the multi-factor etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how physical radiation and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic processing to form DNA adducts and induce genetic mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Contextual Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, including chronic inflammation, two-stage promotion models, and host developmental vulnerability.

topics.label: Methodologies for Assessing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro laboratory methods used to test and establish carcinogenic potential.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture with a summary of environmental cancer risks and a discussion of practical risk-benefit decisions in daily life.
